verses.text: After we said goodbye to them, we set sail and went straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes, and from there we went to Patara.
We found a ship going over to Phoenicia, so we got on board and set sail.
We saw Cyprus and passed it on our left. We sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, because the ship had to unload its cargo there.
We found some followers there and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit, they told Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
When our time was over, we left and went on our way. All of them, with their wives and children, walked with us out of the city. There we knelt on the beach and prayed.
We said goodbye to each other. Then we got on the ship, and they went back home.
We continued our trip from Tyre and landed at Ptolemais. We greeted the believers there and stayed with them for one day.
The next day we left and went to Caesarea. We stayed at the house of Philip, who told people the good news. He was one of the seven helpers.
He had four daughters who were not married, and they prophesied.
We stayed there several days. Then a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

He came to us and took Paul's belt. He tied up his own feet and hands with it and said, "The Holy Spirit says: 'This is how the Jews in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will hand him over to the Gentiles.'"
When we heard this, we and the people there begged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
Then Paul answered, "Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be tied up, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
He would not listen to us, so we stopped and said, "May the Lord's will be done."
After this, we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us. They took us to the home of Mnason, where we would stay. He was from Cyprus, and he was one of the first followers.
When we arrived in Jerusalem, the believers welcomed us gladly.
The next day Paul went with us to see James. All the elders were there.
Paul greeted them and told them, one by one, everything God had done among the Gentiles through his work.
When they heard this, they praised God. Then they said to Paul, "Brother, you see how many thousands of Jews have believed. They all follow the law very strictly.
They have been told that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn away from Moses. They heard you tell them not to circumcise their children and not to follow our customs.
What should we do? They will surely hear that you have come.
So do what we tell you. We have four men here who have made a promise to God.

Take these men and go through the cleansing ceremony with them. Pay their costs so they can shave their heads. Then everyone will know that what they heard about you is not true. They will see that you yourself keep the law.

As for the Gentiles who believe, we have written to them with our decision. They must not eat food offered to idols, or blood, or the meat of strangled animals, and they must stay away from sexual sin."

So the next day Paul took the men and went through the cleansing ceremony with them. Then he went into the temple to tell when the days of cleansing would end, and when the offering would be made for each of them.
When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and grabbed him.

They shouted, "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, our law and this place. And now he has even brought Greeks into the temple and made this holy place unclean!"
They had seen Trophimus from Ephesus with Paul in the city, and they thought Paul had brought him into the temple.
The whole city was in an uproar, and the people came running. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.
While they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the Roman soldiers that all of Jerusalem was in an uproar.
At once he took some officers and soldiers and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
The commander came and arrested Paul. He ordered him to be tied with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
Some people in the crowd shouted one thing and some shouted another. The commander could not find out the truth because of all the noise, so he ordered Paul to be taken into the army building.
When Paul reached the steps, the soldiers had to carry him because the crowd was so violent.
The crowd kept following and shouting, "Kill him!"
As Paul was about to be taken into the army building, he said to the commander, "May I say something to you?" The commander said, "You speak Greek?
Then are you not the Egyptian who started a revolt some time ago? He led four thousand terrorists out into the desert."
Paul answered, "I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia. I am a citizen of an important city. Please let me speak to the people."
The commander gave him permission. So Paul stood on the steps and raised his hand to quiet the people. When they were all silent, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language.
